active_questions.q: What is the current state of work on representing proofs as structured objects, and how does the eight-role proof-graph vocabulary relate to it?
Which further classical proofs contain algorithm capsules, and which domains should the ATAP corpus cover next?
What methods exist for measuring structural similarity between labeled directed graphs, so 'family resemblance' becomes measurable rather than visible?
How have formal methods been applied to biological and other non-mathematical systems, and what did those applications actually yield?

frontier.open: Whether the algorithm-capsule regularity is a real structural feature of mathematics or an artifact of how these three proofs were encoded
Whether the eight-role node vocabulary is adequate as the corpus grows, or will need roles it does not yet have
Whether Mermaid graph representation is right for mathematics, or the most-used method mistaken for the only one
Whether pointing mathematical structure at an under-mathematized domain produces genuine discovery or sophisticated re-description — GLMP being the first test
Whether the graph representation preserves what makes a proof beautiful, or strips exactly that out

method.floor: original quoted full-phrase query, all:"<term>" -- unaffected only for single-word terms; matches the numbers in atap-arxiv-feasibility-2026-08-06.json's in_cat_unwindowed/in_cat column
method.corrected: non-overlapping word-pair chunks, each quoted, ANDed -- e.g. 'formal methods systems biology' -> all:"formal methods" AND all:"systems biology"; unchanged from floor for 1-2 word terms. A heuristic, not ground truth: chunk boundaries are naive (first two words paired, then next two), so it can still undercount a term whose natural phrase break falls elsewhere -- see 'formal methods systems biology' (stays at 0 even corrected, ceiling shows 38 real hits exist).
method.ceiling: AND of every individual unquoted word, no adjacency required at all -- the permissive end, will overcount by picking up papers where the words co-occur without being related; unchanged from floor for 1-word terms
method.scope: in-category (math.LO, cs.LO, cs.PL, math.CT, cs.DM) only, unwindowed only -- the windowed/no-category slices from the original sweep were not re-run since the windowed-vs-unwindowed ratio's direction doesn't depend on the phrase-query defect (both sides of the ratio move together), only its exact magnitude does
method.read_as: floor is a lower bound, ceiling is a loose upper bound with false positives baked in, corrected is a middle estimate using naive phrase chunking -- none of the three is 'the' count. A term at 0/0/0 (e.g. 'qualitative modeling gene regulation') is a real null even under the most permissive construction tested. A term at 0/0/low (e.g. 'proof role vocabulary': 0/0/2) is very likely a real near-null. A term where corrected or ceiling recovers real numbers (e.g. 'model checking biological': 0/18/20) was an instrument artifact, not a finding about the literature.
